Council call (Chairman/Skeptic/Executor + Protocol Steward, User Advocate): add opt-in ?sizing=frame, keep sizing=box as default. Steward: changing the default would change every existing caller's pixels (square tiles become non-square). Skeptic: no caller has asked for a new default. Executor: one parameter, one test. Evidence: live sizing=frame&size=100 -> 158x136 bare, 388x240 amplified, same frame size in both PNGs; box size=200 -> 200x200 with smaller frame. README documents both. Reversal: a consumer that needs one frame size per map and cannot pass sizing=frame.

Council call (Chairman/Skeptic/Executor + User Advocate, Staff Engineer): omit text amplifiers from 3D models, as today; direction now sets the heading. Staff Eng: stroke text does not survive fill extrusion (same cause as frameOnly/bakeIcon). User Advocate: MapLibre/ATAK/Cesium label tracks natively from track data. Documented in README roadmap and amplifiers section (829b79a). Reversal: a 3D client that cannot draw its own labels asks for them -> bake text into the bakeIcon texture.

Council call (Chairman/Skeptic/Executor + Protocol Steward, UI/UX): follow milsymbol and the reference picker; documented in README. Steward: C is an equipment field, B a unit field; one spot by design, so a unit with C is outside the standard's layout. Skeptic: moving C would break the 10-type match against sidc.milsymb.net (amplifier-layout.test.ts). Executor: no code. Reversal: a 2525D/APP-6 figure that shows C on a unit above B, or a real feed that sends quantity on units.

Council call (Chairman/Skeptic/Executor + Protocol Steward, Security): opt-in ?strict=1 answers 400 for both; default unchanged (829b79a). Steward: a default 400 would turn working tags into broken images for existing callers. Security: the 64-char cut stays as the bound either way. Live: strict=1 + 65-char uniqueDesignation -> 400 'Amplifier text longer than 64 characters: uniqueDesignation'; strict=1 unknown SIDC -> 400; without strict both 200. Reversal: callers ask for strict by default, or logs show silent cuts hiding real data loss.
